entertainment.title: 5 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Fire Country
entertainment.summary: Fire Country's small-town heart, family drama, and high stakes rescues are hard to replicate, but here are five shows that capture some of that same spirit.
entertainment.body:
CBS Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Firefighter and EMT shows have been around for decades but have become increasingly popular in recent years thanks to shows like "Chicago Fire," "Station 19," and "9-1-1." CBS launched its latest show in the genre, "Fire Country," in 2022 and set it apart from the competition by introducing audiences to a small town instead of throwing its heroes into a big city and letting the fires and romantic drama cloud the atmosphere.

Edgewater is different. The small, fictional town in "Fire Country" is surrounded by mountains and forest. It's north of San Francisco and prone to wildfires. While reminiscent of Humboldt County and the San Francisco Bay area, Edgewater has an unmistakable Hollywood charm that's all its own. Its fire departments are heavily influenced by families like the Leones, whose son Bode (Max Thieriot) has worked his way from being an inmate in the fictional Cal Fire Three Rock Con Camp to being hired as a legitimate firefighter at Edgewater's Station 42 over the show's five seasons.

Bode's journey is a complicated one involving healing familial wounds, repairing friendships, and, unsurprisingly, finding love amid a lot of trauma. But, between rescuing civilians and homes from fires, the Leones and their loved ones have stories that are grounded in reality and focus on heart. There's a bar where everybody knows each other, firefighter family dinners, and festivals that can only happen in a town where everyone knows the high school quarterback's name. The vibes of "Fire Country" are hard to replicate, but here are five shows to watch if you love escaping to Edgewater.

Disney/Jake Giles Netter "9-1-1: Nashville" is a spinoff of the successful "9-1-1" franchise and shares the country, homey vibes that persist in "Fire Country" even though only one of the shows is set in the South. Firefighting is all in the family on "9-1-1: Nashville," too. Captain Don Hart (Chris O'Donnell) leads fictional Station 113 and works alongside his two sons, Ryan Hart (Michael Provost) and Blue Bennings (Hunter McVey).

The Leones and the Harts have family drama in common, but the Harts' issues have an unmistakable spice that's only found in the "9-1-1" universe. Blue is Don's son with his ex, former backup singer Dixie Bennings (LeAnn Rimes), who is bitter about a lot more than the fact that her career dreams didn't materialize. Her desire to be with Don is also unfulfilled, thanks in large part to Don's wife Blythe (Jessica Capshaw). Rimes adds an almost indescribable touch of Cruella de Vil to her villain performance. Plus, Capshaw plays the uptight, entitled, yet equally calculated foil perfectly, so their rivalry is one of the best parts of the show.

The Bachelor just announced that its upcoming 30th season will have a major twist—tapping Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman as the leading man for the ABC reality dating show.

Nevertheless, Hartman’s huddle couldn’t be more thrilled that he’s passing out petals instead of throwing passes.

“They’re excited,” the 27-year-old revealed of his family’s reaction to the news. “My mom and I have a really cool relationship, and my pops is obviously just supportive. And their big thing is just be myself and enjoy the experience, and you know, trust the instincts and trust your gut.”

Hartman’s casting marks the first time in years the franchise's Bachelor wasn’t picked from the pool of prior Bachelorette contestants—but that’s not the only unique quality Hartman is bringing to the Fantasy Suite.

Below, find a play-by-play of all the X’s and O’s to know about Hartman.

After playing college football at the University of Notre Dame, Hartman was drafted into the United Football League in 2024, playing for the Birmingham Stallions. That same year, he signed with the Washington Commanders as an undrafted free agent.

Hartman has remained a member of the Commanders’ practice squad and acts as their backup quarterback. He has yet to play in a regular season NFL game.

Though the musician turned off comments on her baby news, fans flocked to the replies of her second-most recent post — a roundup of October 2025 snaps from When We Were Young Festival — to share in their surprise.

“I’M SORRY WHAT–,” one person wrote, while another commented, “WHAT THE HELL AVRIL!!!! OMG.”

Clearly, Lavigne is good at keeping her personal life private. In addition to keeping her motherhood journey private, fans still have no idea who the man in her life is. entertainment.body:
IDK brings together a pair of Detroit legends — Eminem and the late J Dilla — for the first time on the rapper’s new single “Welcome.”

Slim Shady contributes the chorus over a hard-edged, choppy Dilla beat while IDK shows off his dark lyricism on the all-Motor City affair; in the music video, IDK is driven around by Nissan, the son of D12 rapper Proof, who collaborated with both Eminem and J Dilla.

entertainment.title: RJ Mitte’s mom ‘trying to navigate’ life one month after ‘Breaking Bad’ star’s death: ‘So painfully difficult’
entertainment.summary: The beloved actor died by suicide on Oct. 12.
entertainment.body:
RJ Mitte’s mother, Dyna Mitte, opened up about the “Breaking Bad” star’s “painfully difficult” death at 34.

“My beautiful boy, it has been a month since you left us. I miss you so much it hurts,” she wrote via Instagram Thursday alongside a photo of her and RJ.

“There are days that it feels like it happen [sic] today, and at times it feels like forever ago. I am trying to navigate through this new life, but it is so painfully difficult. What I would not give to hold you again, see that beautiful smile, laugh at the crazy conversations we had, are [sic] just look at you.”

“I love you forever + time. Please continue to watch over us. With all my love, Mom,” Dyna concluded.

As Page Six previously reported, RJ died by suicide by hanging in Brownsville, Texas, on Oct. 12.

Dyna previously opened up about the moment she learned of the death of her son , who was a disabilities advocate and lived with cerebral palsy .

“I called him at 11 [a.m.],” she told NBC News. “He didn’t answer, so I picked up lunch and went to take it to him, and that’s when I discovered him.”

Dyna told the outlet that her son did not seem to leave a note behind, and that she believes his death may have been a decision made in the “spur of the moment.”

entertainment.title: Jake Bugg Remembers Who He Is on ‘Alamo’
entertainment.summary: The U.K. songwriter takes a long look inward and contemplates what he's had to overcome on a new LP: "To write this album, I had to come out on the other side of it"
entertainment.body:
If you want to get Jake Bugg rolling, bring up English football. Sitting in a room of his London home on a late Friday afternoon just before happy hour, Bugg is beaming as he jokes about Manchester City’s fate and points to both a framed, signed game-used Wayne Rooney Three Lions jersey and a Notts County kit bearing his name on the front. This wasn’t one of those shirts that you can buy and personalize. Rather, Bugg was the club’s kit sponsor, a thrill for the lifelong Notts County fan.

Talking football aside, Bugg, showing up via Zoom, has said in the past that he doesn’t fully like interviews. On this day, that’s certainly not the case. When it comes to speaking about his career, Bugg is in a more contemplative mood.

Specifically, he calls back to moments of isolation, and acknowledges times when he’s been ignored or suppressed. He confronts all of these issues on the new Alamo , his seventh studio album and first non-major-label release. They were difficult emotions and memories to parse, but he insists he’s better off for it. Besides, as Bugg says: “I got a record out of it.”

Looking back at his early music career, which started more as the hobby of a teen growing up in Nottingham and quickly turned into a profession, Bugg knows his experience is vastly different from that of others his age. In 2011, then just 16, he played the BBC Introducing stage at Glastonbury and saw his profile rise through prominent sync placements. Bugg’s first album, his self-titled 2012 debut, drew comparisons to early Bob Dylan, with a gusto similar to the Gallaghers (he’d go on to open for Noel Gallagher’s High Flying Birds).

At the time of its release, Rolling Stone wrote that “ Jake Bugg shows an artist who is crazy fully formed, stepping into a journey that should be worth following.” The album peaked at Number One on the U.K. album charts and at No. 75 on the Billboard 200 . His next album was produced by Rick Rubin, and in the years since, he opened for the Rolling Stones, shared a stage with Johnny Marr and Michael Kiwanuka, and later played guitar on Johnny Blue Skies’ Passage du Desir album. entertainment.title: Ye Lawsuit: Musician Says He Was Locked in Wyoming HS to Write ‘Nebuchadnezzar’ Opera
entertainment.summary: The case, the latest over Ye's troubled 2019 opera, claims the rapper's staffers ignored requests to provide food and water or "unlock the band room doors."
entertainment.body:
Ye (the artist formerly known as Kanye West ) is facing a new lawsuit that claims an opera musician was locked inside a Wyoming high school band room to create his biblical opera Nebuchadnezzar .

In a case filed Wednesday (Nov. 11) in federal court, Chase Taylor claims that the controversial rapper hired him to perform in the show, but later revealed that he would need to compose the entire opera from scratch.

In a strange twist, Taylor alleges the star flew him to a Wyoming high school and that he was not allowed to leave: “Defendants locked the door and ordered Taylor to work until the opera was done.”

“Taylor objected to the abusive conditions and asked defendants (through [a staffer]) to unlock the band room doors, provide sufficient food and water, and provide appropriate time off for the musicians to sleep,” Taylor’s lawyers write in the court filings, obtained by Billboard . “Defendants ignored these requests.”

A spokesman for Ye did not immediately return a request for comment from Billboard on Friday (Nov. 13). The case is a civil lawsuit and the rapper has not been accused of any criminal wrongdoing.

Nebuchadnezzar , based on the based on the biblical story of that ancient king, premiered in November 2019 at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles. The opera, which ran just 45 minutes, was met with negative reviews (the Los Angeles Times called it a “Nebuchadsnoozer” ) and was performed only once.

In his lawsuit, Taylor claims he was hired as a performer in the show, but that West’s plans for the opera were “built of air” — that he had “arranged to monetize the production” but had “failed to prepare the actual opera.”

“After Taylor agreed, he learned the truth: there was no opera. No music, no score, no lyrics, no plan,” his lawyers write. “In their place: a barren room, a few other performers, and a directive to compose, orchestrate, and rehearse an opera from scratch, to be performed in four days.”

entertainment.title: Quentin Tarantino names 2 actresses he fired from ‘Inglourious Basterds’: ‘I don’t owe you jack s–t’
entertainment.summary: One of the actresses was ultimately rehired for the Oscar-nominated 2009 war film after managing to convince Tarantino to give her another chance.
entertainment.body:
Quentin Tarantino has revealed that he fired actresses Mélanie Laurent and Isabelle Huppert from “Inglourious Basterds” before production on the 2009 war film even began.

The filmmaker, 63, discussed the casting decisions in Jay Glennie’s new book, “The Making of Quentin Tarantino’s ‘Inglourious Basterds,'” released on Tuesday.

In the book, Tarantino explained that he fired Laurent, 43, because her table read was “terrible,” adding, “It wasn’t good enough to be terrible,” according to People .

He went on to describe the table read as the “most exciting day of pre-production” for him, noting that it is “the closest I get to seeing the movie for the first time.”

“Up until then, it’s just been me reading all the scenes to myself or to a friend,” he continued, “so a table read with the whole cast is so exciting and so important to me.”

Laurent was ultimately rehired, explaining to Tarantino that she had been sick at the time of the table read and saying, “I will fly myself to Germany and put myself up in a hotel. I know you’re busy, but I will wait until you see me again.”

The French actress managed to convince Tarantino to “turn the clock back” and “return to square one,” agreeing to rehearse with him for three days before she was given back her role as Shosanna Dreyfus.

“Let me just go on the record for everybody to know: I love Mélanie,” Tarantino said in the book. “The fact of the matter is, if we were not talking about the making of ‘Inglourious Basterds,’ I would never think about the table read again, for the simple reason Mélanie is my Shosanna. She did a wonderful job.”

entertainment.body:
The "Sk8er Boi" musician recently shared a major glimpse into her private world, confirming she is now a mom after welcoming her first child, a baby girl.

"Our mini f--king princess," she captioned a Nov. 13 Instagram post featuring photos of her holding her daughter, three pairs of vans as well as her hand and another holding their baby's finger, "has arrived.”

Prior to expanding her family, over the years, Lavigne, 42—who hasn't shared details about the identity of her baby's father—has kept her personal life close to the vest.

Before tying the knot with now-ex Chad Kroeger , she was married to Sum 41 alum Deryck Whibley for three years until 2009, ending their relationship on amicable terms.

"Deryck and I have been together for 6-and-a-half years,” she wrote on her website at the time. “We have been friends since I was 17, started dating when I was 19, and married when I was 21. I am grateful for our time together, and I am grateful and blessed for our remaining friendship."

"I admire Deryck and have a great amount of respect for him,” she continued. “He is the most amazing person I know and I love him with all my heart. Deryck and I are separating and moving forward on a positive note.”

And when she met Kroger in 2012, she ultimately decided that she wanted to be more than just his girlfriend, with the couple exchanging vows just a year later. However, by 2015, her relationship with the Nickelback singer met a different ending.

"It is with [a] heavy heart that Chad and I announce our separation today,” she wrote on social media at the time. “Through not only the marriage, but the music as well, we've created many unforgettable moments. We are still, and forever will be, the best of friends, and will always care deeply for each other. To all our family, friends and fans, thank you sincerely for the support."

entertainment.title: Taylor Swift to Perform at the 2026 CMA Awards
entertainment.summary: The superstar singer-songwriter had indicated she'd attend the show, where she's nominated for her 'Toy Story 5' song "I Knew It, I Knew You."
entertainment.body:
The superstar singer-songwriter, who’d indicated when nominations were announced that she’d attend the country music awards show, is not only attending but performing at the 2026 CMA Awards .

Swift previously appeared at the ceremony, known as Country Music’s Biggest Night, a decade ago and last performed there 13 years ago.

Swift is a two-time CMA Entertainer of the Year, becoming the youngest ever winner of that honor in 2009, and in 2013 received the Pinnacle Award. She’s nominated this year for single of the year for her Toy Story 5 song “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which is seen as a top contender for a song of the year Oscar nomination. Swift’s performance at the CMA Awards will take place two days after the 2026 Grammy nominations are announced, where Swift is expected to be a top contender both for “I Knew It, I Knew You” and The Life of a Showgirl , which was released after the end of Grammys eligibility last year.

Swift was also recently announced as the recipient of The Hollywood Reporter ‘s prestigious Sherry Lansing Leadership Award , which she’ll accept at THR ‘s 2026 Women in Entertainment gala.

“I Knew It, I Knew You” marks a return to Swift’s country music roots after a number of pop albums in recent years. So it’s fitting she’s also returning to the CMA Awards for this nomination. She first attended the CMA Awards in 2006 and performed “Red” with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss at the 2013 CMA Awards. In 2016, her last appearance at the CMA Awards, she presented Garth Brooks with his Entertainer of the Year honor.

When this year’s CMA Awards nominations were announced, Swift posted to her Instagram Stories , “LOOKS LIKE I HAVEN’T YEE’D MY LAST HAW THANK YOU CMA!!!! See you there Nov. 18 🤠.”

The 60th annual CMA Awards will be hosted by Lainey Wilson for the third year in a row. The awards show will air live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+ and will be available to stream the next day on Hulu.

entertainment.title: Stephen King Threw ‘Carrie’ in the Trash. Then It Changed Everything
entertainment.summary: On the film’s 50th anniversary, King looks back at the nearly discarded pages, the bargain-basement movie deal and the 1976 classic that transformed horror.
entertainment.body:
In the early 1970s, Stephen King was a struggling and frustrated English teacher in Maine with a wife, two small children and a stack of bills that seemed to be growing much faster than his literary career. During the day, he taught teenagers at Hampden Academy. At night, he’d pound out short stories and quickie tales of terror for lower-tier skin magazines like Cavalier and Adam . The pay wasn’t much, but it kept the lights on … barely. “Two hundred dollars,” says King of his typical fee at the time. “Once in a while, it was $500. That was a huge payday. That bought a lot of groceries.” Things were so tight that the Kings didn’t even have a telephone. Related Stories TV Streaming Ratings Take on a Halloween Vibe With 'Crystal Lake,' 'Carrie' TV Streaming Ratings: 'Carrie' Has a Bloody Good Opening Week

Then, in 1972, King began tinkering with an idea about a painfully awkward teenage girl who is mercilessly bullied by her classmates and terrorized at home by her religiously fanatical mother. When the girl discovers that she possesses telekinetic powers, she finally has a way to strike back. The story would reach its cathartic crescendo at her high school prom, where a horrifically cruel prank involving a bucket of pig’s blood turns what should have been the best night of her young life into an apocalyptic bloodbath. Her name was Carrie White.

Although he had no way of knowing it at the time, the book he had just begun writing would change the course of his life. And not just his. The 1976 movie adaptation of Carrie would turn Sissy Spacek into a bona fide star, give Brian De Palma his first box office hit and pull off something scary movies almost never did, then or now: crash the Oscars. It would also mark the beginning of one of the most prolific — and lucrative — pipelines in movie history, with King’s stories adapted for the screen more than 60 times. Fifty years, several remakes, a notorious Broadway musical and one brand-new Prime Video series later, Carrie White’s bloody fingerprints are still everywhere you look.

The inspiration for the novel that would become Carrie came from several places. Years earlier, while working as a school janitor, King had cleaned the girls’ locker room and noticed the sanitary napkin dispensers mounted on the walls. He began imagining a teenage girl experiencing her first period in the shower with no understanding of what was happening to her while her classmates responded with ridicule. He combined that image with his interest in telekinesis and his memories of two girls he’d known growing up who had been treated as social pariahs. “I wasn’t bullied,” King says. “I think that every kid feels a little bit bullied in school, but I had less of it than others.” The girls, however, weren’t as fortunate. “They were savagely bullied about their clothes, about their hair, just about their lack of social graces. They were country kids and they were really treated poorly.”

entertainment.title: David Walliams Under Investigation by U.K. Police Over Alleged “Serious Sexual Offenses”
entertainment.summary: It comes just days after Walliams was accused of sexual assault and grooming in a bombshell Guardian and ITV News investigation, claims he vehemently denies.
entertainment.body:
David Walliams , the BAFTA-winning comedian and bestselling children’s author, is under investigation by London’s Metropolitan Police over “alleged serious sexual offenses.”

BBC News has reported that the Met investigation is separate from the bombshell accusations Walliams faces in a joint report by ITV News and The Guardian released this week. The Met said it had “received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s… Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers,” the statement added. Related Stories Movies From Sandworms to 007: Joe Walker on 'Dune: Part Three,' Villeneuve, McQueen and Bond Movies 'One Sweet Hour': One Aging Elvis Impersonator. One Monk. Two Estranged Irish Brothers Facing Trauma.

Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney urged anyone who has been a victim of a sexual offence to “come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.” He continued: “We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process.”

Tuesday’s report detailed accusations of sexual assault and grooming by several women, some of whom allege they were as young as 15 when the interactions took place.

Walliams, best known for roles in Little Britain , Come Fly With Me and as a judge on Britain’s Got Talent , had sought an injunction to prevent the two news organizations from publishing his identity, over fears that he would be “highly likely” to kill himself. He maintained that the suicide risk is not attributed to any wrongdoing but to what his lawyers described as “trial by media.” His lawyers have said that Walliams has already tried to take his own life twice.

The injunction request was later rejected by a High Court judge, after which the British press has been free to publish Walliams’ identity.

He vehemently denied the allegations and told ITV News and The Guardian: “I am not a sexual predator… I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me. […] Looking back, I realize that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with. I realize I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.”

entertainment.title: Savannah Guthrie Extends ‘Today’ Show Deal

entertainment.body:
Savannah Guthrie has extended her contract with NBC News , The Hollywood Reporter has confirmed. Guthrie’s contract was set to expire at the end of the year.

Guthrie, the popular co-anchor of NBC’s Today show, has been the news as much as she’s reported the news this year. In the early morning hours of Feb. 1, 2026, Guthrie’s mom Nancy Guthrie was kidnapped from her Tucson, Arizona home. Nancy Guthrie is presumed dead though her remains have never been found. Nancy was 84 years old and in poor health. She did not have her necessary medication with her. Related Stories TV The Other Midterms Flip: Broadcast Networks, Led by NBC, Dominated Election Night Coverage TV Carson Daly Named Co-Anchor of NBC's 'Saturday Today'

On Feb. 10, doorbell footage of a masked man approaching her home on the night of her disappearance was made public. No suspect was ever identified.

A pair of notes from the purported kidnapper(s) were sent to local news outlets. The first demanded Bitcoin for Nancy’s safe return; the second note did not demand money but stated that Nancy died shortly after her abduction.

The second note reads, in full: “Guthrie Family, We did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this and hope you can all find peace. We are truly sorry.”

Savannah Guthrie returned to work at the NBC morning show in April. Craig Melvin is her Today show co-anchor.

Guthrie is set to co-host the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade with her usual collaborators Hoda Kotb and Al Roker. This Thanksgiving marks the 100th anniversary of the procession. The Macy’s march actually began in 1924, but it took a three-year hiatus during World War II.

entertainment.title: Jason Voorhees Is Back for More Blood: the 13th ‘Friday the 13th’ Film Is Coming
entertainment.summary: The 2027 film will be directed by Friday the 13th veteran Steve Miner, who played a pivotal role in shaping the murderous character through the introduction of his mask and machete
entertainment.body:
The 13th installment of the Friday the 13th film franchise has been announced on Friday, Nov. 13, marking the first scheduled release in the horror series in almost 20 years.

Jason Voorhees is back for more blood in a script from newcomer David Fliegel. The film will be directed by Friday the 13th veteran Steve Miner, who played a pivotal role in shaping the murderous character in the second and third installments of the franchise, released in 1981 and 1982, respectively. The machete and mask introduced in those early releases have become his most iconic identifiers.

“When I put the hockey mask on Jason for Friday the 13th Part III , I knew it would create a truly scary image that would work for that movie,” Miner said. “I had no idea that it would live on as one of the most iconic symbols in horror films. I’m thrilled to come back and continue the legacy.”

entertainment.title: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Unearths $1.5M in Box Office Previews
entertainment.summary: Paramount's spooky take on 'A Christmas Carol' debuts opposite 'How to Rob a Bank' and 'Ghost Soldier.'
entertainment.body:
Johnny Depp ‘s push for a career comeback is underway at the box office with the holiday-themed ghost story Ebenezer .

Paramount Pictures releases Ebenezer in more than 3,500 North American theaters on Friday, with the movie grossing $1.5 million from Thursday previews. The studio projects director Ti West’s spooky adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol to collect $20 million domestically and add another $20 million internationally from 63 worldwide markets. Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley and Ian McKellen round out the cast for the $38 million-budgeted feature that stars Depp as the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge.

Ebenezer marks Depp’s return to studio fare following negative headlines surrounding his and ex-wife Amber Heard ‘s messy 2022 defamation trial and abuse allegations that Depp has denied. His most recent studio release was 2018’s Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald , as Warner Bros. dropped him from that franchise two years later after the actor lost a libel suit against the publisher of The Sun .

The film has divided critics, as it holds a 52 percent approval from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Frank Scheck declares that Ebenezer “fulfills its ostensible goal of restoring the actor to A-list status.”

Another major release is Amazon MGM Studios’ How to Rob a Bank , hitting 2,810 domestic theaters. Filmmaker David Leitch’s heist movie nabbed $900,000 in previews and is expected to launch in the high single digits in North America against a $40 million budget.

How to Rob a Bank has come up a bit empty with critics, holding a 33 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, with THR chief film critic David Rooney noting in his review that “the fun wears a bit thin.” Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz and Anna Sawai lead the ensemble cast for the movie about a group of bank robbers who document their exploits on social media.

Sony Pictures released Ghost Soldier in 2,558 North American locations on Wednesday, with director William Eubank’s action movie grossing $3.1 million over the two days, including Tuesday previews. The studio projects a $6 million five-day opening for the film that stars Jim Caviezel as a former Green Beret who must defend his Wyoming community against a corporate threat. Hailing from Mandalay Pictures, Ghost Soldier holds a 42 score from Rotten Tomatoes critics and a 90 from audiences.

entertainment.title: Bono Says Dolly Parton ‘Sang Herself to Some Other Place’ on the New U2 Song ‘Torn’: ‘It Feels Like a Prayer … For America’
entertainment.summary: The "sci-fi country" ballad featuring Parton's final vocal performance, closes the band's new album, Carnaval de Luz .
entertainment.body:
In life, Dolly Parton always looked for ways to bring people together. In death, it seems, her work carries on. The members of U2 sat on the Jimmy Kimmel Live! couch on Thursday night (Nov. 12) to discuss their new album , Carnaval de Luz , whose final track, “ Torn ,” features the last-ever vocals recorded by Parton, who died at 80 on Aug. 25 after a brief battle with cancer. Related Aria Vega Wins Best New Artist at the 2026 Latin Grammys: 'Dreams Know No Fear' On Winning First Latin Grammy, Camila Fernández Thanks Expectant Baby for 'Strength to be Here' 50 Cent Trolls Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Affair With 'P.I.M.P.' Music Video AI Deepfake: 'Jensen Don't Sweat It' Explore Bono Dolly Parton U2 See latest videos, charts and news

“Is there anyone else that the whole world is going to agree upon other than Dolly?,” Bono said about the universal outpouring of love and devotion that followed Parton’s passing earlier this year. “Dolly Parton is a mythical figure who actually existed recently,” he continued. “And our hearts are broken by this, but we are also blessed to be given her last vocal.”

Bono said the group very much wanted to work with Parton and they pitched her a few ideas, including a kind of “folky” thing called “Lifelong” that he described as a “dizzy, drunken marriage song.” Dipping into his best/worst Tennessee accent, Bono said Parton told the group that it was perhaps, “‘a little too Irish for me if that’s okay.'”

Instead, Parton said she had a song she’d started and was happy to let U2 tinker, adding that she was excited to see where they’d take it. “The implication here, of course, is, ‘if I don’t like where you take it, it will never see the light of day,'” Bono said of Parton’s thrown gauntlet. Guitarist The Edge said it was a “real shock” that Parton was willing to put her musical destiny in their hands because they were aiming for something kind of “sci-fi country” and she was really game to play along.

In the end, Bono called the experience a master class, recalling being blown away by Parton’s range as she “sang herself to some other place” on the tune. “We are told that she did not know that she was that ill. But it’s her last prayer in a way … was this song,” Bono said. “It feels like a prayer, and I think it’s for America, but I think it’s for anywhere where there’s a divided politics.”

The meditative track opens with Parton’s plaintive vocals as she wonders, “What am I supposed to do?/ And how am I supposed to choose?/ I love them both and I just feel so torn.”

entertainment.title: Streaming Ratings: ‘From’ Dominates an Otherwise Quiet Halloween Week
entertainment.summary: The sci-fi/horror series is the only title to draw more than a billion minutes of watch time.
entertainment.body:
Logo text The last week of October was a relatively quiet one on Nielsen’s streaming charts, with one big exception.

From , the MGM+ show that was added to Netflix’s library on Oct. 19, spent its second straight week as the No. 1 overall title. The series drew 2.04 billion minutes of watch time, up 24 percent week to week . From also surpassed the mark it set a week earlier for the most viewing minutes for an acquired series this year.

Beyond From , however, there weren’t a lot of highlights. No other series or movie cracked the billion-minute mark. The top 10 overall titles combined for 9.03 billion minutes of viewing, down from 9.22 billion the previous week.

Netflix’s Nobody Wants This (847 million minutes) led the original series top 10. The comedy was up about 17 percent week to week but once again trailed its performance from a year ago. In the two weeks after season three’s Oct. 22 premiere, Nobody Wants This has totaled 1.57 billion viewing minutes, off about 14 percent from 1.83 billion minutes for the same time frame after season two’s debut last year.

Love Is Blind (796 million minutes), VisionQuest (548 million) and Tulsa King (501 million) all posted small week to week improvements. Netflix’s Lupin (579 million) had the week’s best premiere, and the short docuseries The One About Matthew Perry had 541 million minutes of viewing.

Hocus Pocus rose to the top of the movie rankings during Halloween week, scoring 405 million minutes of viewing on Disney+. The Nightmare Before Christmas, Coraline, Coco and Hocus Pocus 2 also made the top 10.

entertainment.title: Christian Cousins, Young Actor in ‘Knots Landing’ and ‘Kindergarten Cop,’ Dies at 43
entertainment.summary: He and his identical twin, Joseph, shared roles as Bobby Ewing on the CBS show and as Penelope Ann Miller’s son in the Arnold Schwarzenegger movie.
entertainment.body:
Christian Cousins, who with his identical twin brother shared roles as youngsters on the CBS primetime soap Knots Landing and in the Arnold Schwarzenegger film Kindergarten Cop , has died. He was 43.

Cousins died Oct. 20 after a battle with liver disease, his half-brother Jonas Roeser announced on Instagram. “He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams,” he wrote.

Christian and twin brother Joseph were not yet 4 when they first appeared on Knots Landing as Bobby Ewing during the show’s ninth season in 1987, and they wound up on 57 episodes through 1992. Related Stories TV Michael John Roberts, Animator and 'BoJack Horseman' and 'TripTank' Director, Dies at 48 TV Dan Hicks, NBC Sports Play-by-Play Legend, Dies at 64

Bobby, who had a twin sister, Betsy, was named by Joan Van Ark’s Valene Ewing after the character played by Patrick Duffy on Dallas was run over by a car driven by Morgan Brittany’s Katherine Wentworth. ( Knots Landing was a spinoff of Dallas , and producers there were fond of series crossovers and piggybacking off its Lorimar sibling.)

In Kindergarten Cop (1990), directed by Ivan Reitman, Christian and Joseph portrayed Dominic, one of the students taught by Schwarzenegger’s John Kimble, an L.A. detective working undercover at an elementary school. Dominic’s mom is played by Penelope Ann Miller, and he winds up as a hostage.

Christian Michail Cousins and Joseph were born on March 17, 1983, and raised in Orange County, California.

After embarking on Knots Landing — their character was introduced on a November 1984 episode in which Val gives birth to Bobby and Betsy and then they’re kidnapped, resulting in a season-long storyline — Christian and Joseph shared roles on episodes of Father Dowling Mysteries , Eerie, Indiana and Intruders and in Critters 3 (1991).

They played twins named Hope and Faith on a 1988 episode of Highway to Heaven and brothers named Bradley and Steven in Twin Sitters (1995).

entertainment.title: Christian Cousins, Kindergarten Cop Actor, Dead at 43
entertainment.summary: A former child actor is gone too soon. Christian Cousins—who starred alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Kindergarten Cop in the ‘90s—died in October, his brother Jonas Roeser confirmed on social...
entertainment.body:
Christian Cousins —who starred alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Kindergarten Cop in the ‘90s— died in October, his brother Jonas Roeser confirmed on social media. He was 43.

“It’s hard to share that my brother, Christian Cousins, has passed away,” Jonas captioned an Oct. 22 Instagram post , within which he noted that he connected with Christian and his twin brother Joseph Cousins later in life. “They grew up in California while I was in Washington and I didn’t get to know them until I was in college. Before that, I grew up watching them on television in Knots Landing and the lead role of Dominic in Kindergarten Cop with Arnold Schwarzenegger.”

“But those roles are only a small part of how I’ll remember Christian,” Jonas continued. “He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams.”

He noted that Christian had been battling liver disease, though he did not share additional information.

“It brings me comfort to believe he is now in heaven with his mother, free from the pain he was carrying,” Jonas concluded. “Rest easy, Christian. I hope your soul is at rest and that you’ve found peace. You are my brother and you will be missed.”

Christian and his twin Joseph shared the role of Dominic in the 1990 film Kindergarten Cop , which saw Arnold play LAPD detective John Kimble, who is forced to go undercover as a kindergarten teacher.

In addition to the beloved film, Christian appeared in the series Knot’s Landing as Bobby Gibson Ewing, again sharing the role with Joseph, and had credits on 1991’s Critters 3 , 1992’s Intruders and Twin Sitters in 1994.

He pivoted away from acting, however, and in 2020­—during a virtual reunion with Arnold and the cast of Kindergarten Cop —revealed an executive for a furniture business and co-owned a CBD company.

entertainment.title: Morgan Freeman Gambled With The Devil On A Classic Twilight Zone Episode
entertainment.summary: Morgan Freeman was still a relative unknown when he played cards with Satan himself in a segment of the '80s revival of "The Twilight Zone."
entertainment.body:
Tony (Freeman), Pete (M. Emmet Walsh), Jake (Garrett Morris), Nick (Dan Hedaya), and Marty (Barney Martin) are playing poker at Pete's house. Everything seems to be perfectly normal at first (apart from the fact that the fridge is empty). Nick, who is filling in for his cousin Norman (allegedly), is revealed to be the devil. Making it clear he plans on leaving with a soul, he challenges them to a card game, with the loser accompanying him back to Hell.

CBS Despite being directed by Wes Craven and centering on a game of cards with the devil, "Dealer's Choice" is actually quite humorous. While the four men are clearly worried when Nick claims to be none other than Satan, they all maintain a sarcastic and slightly deadpan attitude, making for a darkly funny segment. For example, the subject of who gets to have the loser's bowling bowl comes up, and after Nick refuses to reveal who he'll take, Jake tells him, "It's one thing being the devil, it's another thing being a total jerk!"

While it doesn't belong to any of the best episodes from the '80s revival , it's still a memorable segment, and not just because Morgan Freeman is in it. Dan Hedaya's performance as the prince of darkness is great; a subtle departure from many satanic portrayals. Nick is physically and conversationally an average joe, and that's part of what makes him so unnerving. He ultimately leaves empty handed when his trickery is discovered, but not before conjuring a parting gift — a fridge full of beer for the poker buddies.

entertainment.title: Robyn Slams Eurovision: ‘It’s So Embarrassing’
entertainment.summary: "After watching it, I feel overstimulated in a bad way," the pop star said.
entertainment.body:
While speaking to Amy Poehler on the latest episode of the comedian’s Good Hang podcast, which dropped Nov. 10, the Swedish pop star did not hold back when asked for her thoughts on the 70-year-old international song competition. “Oof,” Robyn began.

“I mean, we don’t have ABBA anymore, so I don’t really watch Eurovision ,” she continued, informing Poehler that the Swedish quartet indeed won Eurovision in 1974 with Billboard Hot 100 No. 6 smash “Waterloo.” “Hard to beat.”

“Then we had Carola [Häggkvist], both me and Zara [Larsson] grew up listening to her — amazing artist,” Robyn continued. “Now it’s just s–t … It’s so embarrassing. It really is embarrassing.”

She added, “After watching it, I feel overstimulated in a bad way.”

The interview came shortly before the Coachella 2027 lineup was announced . The annual music festival features Robyn on a bill headlined by SZA, Dua Lipa and Tame Impala. She’ll play on both Saturdays of the two-weekend festival, as will Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, ADÉLA, Role Model and — funnily enough — Måneskin, which won Eurovision in 2021 with “”Zitti e Buoni.”

Though the “Dancing on My Own” singer didn’t get into specifics on what she doesn’t like about Eurovision , she’s far from the first to criticize the televised European Broadcast Union competition in recent years. Multiple countries withdrew from this year’s iteration after Eurovision announced that Israel would be permitted to compete, despite the country’s war on Hamas killing tens of thousands of Palestinians over the last three years in what the United Nations has characterized as a genocide, which Israel denies.

Robyn’s most recent album, Sexistentialism , dropped in March, peaking at No. 7 on the Billboard T op Dance Albums chart.

entertainment.body:
Mickey Mouse is channeling his inner-Kevin McAllister this holiday season in the new Disney Christmas special Mickey’s Home Alone .

Below, Billboard Family is premiering the exclusive “Ho-Ho-Home for Christmas” music video from the special, which arrives Thanksgiving day (Nov. 26) on Disney Jr. and streams next day on Disney+. In the music video, Mickey can’t wait to celebrate Christmas with Minnie Mouse and the rest of the gang at their cozy home. entertainment.title: Remembering Shane MacGowan’s ‘Beautiful Chaos’: Inside a Star-Packed New Tribute Comp
entertainment.summary: Tom Waits, Dropkick Murphys, the Jesus and Mary Chain, and others explain why they recorded songs for 20th Century Paddy
entertainment.body:
Shane MacGowan ’s funeral was both a farewell to a cherished icon and a spectacular tribute concert . Nick Cave performed the Pogues ’ “A Rainy Night in Soho,” Glen Hansard and Lisa O’Neill duetted on “Fairytale of New York,” and the surviving members of the Pogues raised “The Parting Glass,” an Irish folk song they recorded in 1985. The service, held shortly after MacGowan’s death in December 2023, toasted the talent of a songwriter whose legacy was making Irish folk music improbably hip. Among those attending were Irish President Michael D. Higgins, Bono, Primal Scream’s Bobby Gillespie, controversial Irish politician Gerry Adams, Johnny Depp, and Game of Thrones actor Aidan Gillen.

For MacGowan’s widow, Victoria Mary Clarke, the send-off was transcendent. “It was like he was just on the roof of the church looking down, beaming this energy into everybody,” she says on a Zoom from her home, where she’s surrounded by her own colorful paintings. “I felt it and I got up and danced, and I felt him celebrating.”

Watching her husband’s friends interpret his music at the funeral moved her profoundly. “It felt like that was something I’d like to have a record of,” she says. She also loved hearing other renditions of his music at a 2024 tribute concert held in New York. So she started making calls to see how many artists would contribute cover songs to a MacGowan tribute record. She ended up with enough music for three LPs.

The album, 20th Century Paddy – The Songs of Shane MacGowan , comes out today and demonstrates the late singer-songwriter’s range. After emerging from the dark streets of London during punk’s first boom (when he fronted the Nips), MacGowan drew inspiration from Irish reels and music-hall ballads and infused them with punk spirit as a member of the Pogues and, later, as frontman for his own band, the Popes. The repertoire for both bands was a mix of traditional folk songs and MacGowan’s originals, which reflected his equal loves of Irish literature and tin whistles. Blessed with a crock of gold to choose from, Clarke pared the track list down to three LPs’ worth of music, with songs from every point of MacGowan’s career performed by a roster of artists who appreciate MacGowan’s musical perspective. The Jesus and Mary Chain ’s Jim Reid recalls the surprise of first hearing MacGowan’s blend of influences: “To me, it sounded like punk music,” he says. “Once you’d heard it, you’d think, ‘Why hadn’t that happened sooner?’”

entertainment.title: Jack White on the Magic of Loretta Lynn and ‘Van Lear Rose’: ‘Outstanding and Life-Affirming’
entertainment.summary: The country music legend’s Grammy-winning 2004 album returns to streaming and gets a newly remastered reissue on White’s Third Man Records
entertainment.body:
Even over two decades later, Jack White still can’t believe it actually happened.

Sitting in a bright office back in his hometown of Detroit, White is reflecting on Van Lear Rose , Loretta Lynn ‘s award-winning 2004 album that he produced, and that helped bring a whole new generation of fans not just to the queen of Butcher Holler, Kentucky, but to the genre of country music itself.

“I could talk about this record forever and not get bored with it,” White says, getting close to tears numerous times. Today, the brilliant Van Lear Rose gets another life with a newly remastered reissue (alongside an additional track, “Just to Have You Back”) via White’s Third Man Records , also returning to streaming for the first time in seven years. Its impact, though, has never wavered.

When Van Lear Rose was released in 2004, mainstream country music was fresh off a post-9/11 shift: artists like the Chicks and Shania Twain fell off playlists to make way for patriotic-skewed , male-dominated lineups. Though some modern legends, like Johnny Cash, were undergoing a cultural resurgence , the genre was nowhere close to a mainstream embrace. Country may be “cool” now, but two decades ago it was far more often the butt of stereotypes and cheap jokes.

White, however, was a longtime Lynn fan. The White Stripes album White Blood Cells was dedicated to her, and he and bandmate Meg White had routinely covered her song “Rated X” in live shows. Lynn had even invited the duo out to her home in Hurricane Mills, Tennessee, to thank them, cooking homemade chicken and dumplings, and chatting around the kitchen table. It was a transformative experience for them all. “[Lynn] went up to the attic and got Meg a red dress,” White says. “Meg was crying, we couldn’t believe it. It was so kind of her to do that and embrace us. We were nowhere near the neighborhood of someone she should know about and care about.”

As they ate, Lynn casually mentioned that she might want to make another record soon. White remembers throwing his name in the ring. “I put my hand up like some ridiculous notion while I’m eating chicken, saying, ‘Well, if you ever need a producer for that record, just give me a holler,’” he recalls. “I’m thinking, ‘no fucking way they were going to pick me. Are you kidding me? This is in Nashville.’ And Loretta did, and she trusted me somehow.”

entertainment.title: Iron Maiden’s Nicko McBrain Recalls Spinal Tap Moments Touring for ‘Somewhere in Time’
entertainment.summary: Read a hilarious excerpt from the drummer’s new book, Hello Boys and Girls!
entertainment.body:
Forty years ago this fall, Iron Maiden released their sixth album, Somewhere in Time , which became an instant classic thanks to the singles “Wasted Years” and “Stranger in a Strange Land.” About a year had passed since they’d concluded their gargantuan World Slavery Tour, which had made them metal superstars, so they worked hard to find ways of making a run of shows they dubbed Somewhere on Tour even more over-the-top.

An excerpt from Maiden drummer Nicko McBrain’s newly released book, Hello Boys and Girls! , highlights some of the right and wrong turns they made while making the album and on tour. Elsewhere in the book, he also tells his life story, both before joining Maiden in 1982, his time in the group, and after he decided to step away from touring with the band in 2024 due to the aftereffects of a stroke a year earlier.

Diehard Maiden fans will instantly recognize McBrain’s voice when they read the book, especially since “Hello boys and girls” was his catchphrase. He refers affectionately to bassist/bandleader Steve Harris as “’’Arry” and guitarist Adrian Smith as “H” and shares anecdotes about singer Bruce Dickinson and guitarist Dave Murray. (His use of ’kin’ should make sense if you read it out loud.)

Here’s what he wrote in the book about the period surrounding Somewhere in Time , beginning with the initial writing sessions for the album, which took place in the Bahamas .

Bruce clearly thought the band needed to go in a different direction and turned up to Nassau with a bunch of acoustic songs. ’Arry thought he’d lost the plot, and rather than getting us all in and saying, “What do you boys think?” he rejected them on the spot.

I could tell that Bruce was a bit miffed about that, but it was ’Arry’s band and he called the shots. I never heard Bruce’s efforts, but ’Arry said they were quite Jethro Tull, and while I’ve got nothing against Jethro Tull (we’d actually covered their song “Cross-Eyed Mary”), they’re definitely not very Maiden. entertainment.title: How to Become (and Stay) a Movie Star in 2026
entertainment.summary: A role on a hit YA rom-com can get you started. Just don’t do it twice.
entertainment.body:
One of Hollywood’s favorite subjects to pontificate on over business lunches — landing somewhere between the latest layoffs and who should really be cast as the next James Bond — is the state of the movie star. Where to find them? How to make them? Do they even still matter?

In our annual Next Gen issue — which celebrates the future leaders of the entertainment industry, offscreen and on — The Hollywood Reporter has been doing our part to answer these questions, identifying a new crop of stars yearly. To compile this list , we trust our own instincts, certainly, but also survey executives, creatives and producers about the talent who excites them. This is how we tapped Sydney Sweeney well before her Euphoria fame and Glen Powell years ahead of his Top Gun ascent. More recently, we featured David Jonsson, who this summer stood on the Comic-Con stage taking on the mantle of Black Panther .

Since the beginning of the industry itself, Hollywood has always relied on a steady stream of youthful stars to put in front of the entertainment-imbibing masses, from Clara Bow to James Dean to the Brat Pack. The talent both dictated and fulfilled the needs of the current moment.

While Hollywood continues to slash content spends and M&A is laying waste to legacy studios, a potent combination of market forces and audience interests is working in favor of a certain type of young star. Despite all the turmoil, 2026 is actually a pretty good time to be an upwardly mobile talent. Call it entertainment’s very own K-curve.

But young stardom is achieved in 2026 in a much different way than even 10 years ago. In the late 2010s, IP begot stars, as was the case with Spider-Man initially catapulting the careers of Tom Holland and Zendaya in 2017. There was also a well-worn path where an auteur director could tap a talent, and then the film festival and awards circuit would cement their status, as was the case with Timothée Chalamet in Luca Guadagnino’s Call Me by Your Name .

Then there was the prestige TV contingent. Anya Taylor-Joy had worked steadily in indie movies but only landed at the top of studio wish lists following the success of Netflix’s The Queen’s Gambit , while Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones had Hulu’s much-watched Normal People to thank for their rise.

As of late, a new class of stars has emerged, fully formed and ready for domination, from the recent spate of young adult series. Shows like The Summer I Turned Pretty , Sterling Point and Off Campus engendered fervent fan bases, building audiences for their leads seemingly overnight and creating immediate industry appeal for stars like Lola Tung and Stephen Kalyn, both a part of the Next Gen class of 2026. And while it may be difficult to remember a time before the omnipresence of Heated Rivalry , it has only been a year since that hockey show debuted, and leads Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams have leapfrogged to a level of fame that yields appearances everywhere from the Golden Globes to the Winter Olympics to a Monopoly Board.

sports.title: Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance instead of pushing Jameis Winston's tush on key play
sports.summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance and didn't participate in the play on a key short-yardage snap late in the Giants' loss on Thursday night.
sports.body:
With the Giants leading 21-17 and 3:56 remaining in the fourth quarter on Thursday night, they faced a third-and-1 and sent Jameis Winston in for a quarterback sneak. A first down would have given the Giants a great chance at a long, clock-draining drive. Instead they were stopped, punted, and ended up losing.

As Winston plowed into the line, Skattebo was behind him and could have run in to try to push him forward to gain a yard. Instead, Skattebo stayed in his stance , and by the time he actually got involved in the play, the Commanders had stopped Winston’s forward progress.

It’s unclear why Skattebo didn’t do anything, and he wasn’t asked about it after the game. But at a time when every team in the league is well aware of the value of teammates pushing the quarterback forward on sneaks, it was a bizarre play, and one that proved costly for the Giants.

sports.title: New Jags Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates will sit out Sunday's game vs. Titans

sports.body:
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen told reporters in his Friday press conference that safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis will sit out Sunday’s matchup against the Titans because they did not have a bye week with their previous teams. Davon Godchaux, who did have a bye, is set to play.

“Want to be able to make sure [that with] player safety, putting them in a position to succeed, also learn the system, and just give those guys a week to be able to do that,” Coen said.

Coen added that the club had been talking about doing that this week and made the final decision to rest the players on Friday.

The head coach has been impressed with all of the acquisitions so far.

“Yeah, I mean, Jesse Bates has been here until about 10:30 every night, which has been pretty cool seeing him in there learning, grinding, working through it,” Coen said. “There’s obviously so much that safeties have to be able to communicate and operate with in the backend of the entire structure. I’ve really appreciated the way him, Jordan, and Davon have all gone through the work week. Obviously, Davon and Jesse have been through different organizations, teams, moves — this is new for Jordan. And he’s worked his tail off with the strength and conditioning and sports science, athletic training guys this week. And he’s putting his best foot forward to hopefully be able to get out next week for us.”

The Jaguars will be on the road to face the Giants in Week 11, where Davis and Bates will make their respective debuts.

sports.title: Troy Aikman engages in potential pre-tampering with Kyle Shanahan
sports.summary: If Troy Aikman exits broadcasting after this season (last month, he put the chance at "50-50") and if Aikman lands a key position in a front office, the name at the top of his head-coaching wishlist will already be known.
sports.body:
Via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing , Aikman said during a Thursday appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas that, if he were running an NFL team, he would try to hire 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan.

“I’ve been asked a lot of questions here, certainly over the last several weeks, about any aspirations that I may have of going in a front office,” Aikman said. “Or ‘Who would you hire as your head coach?’ If I was in a position to hire someone as a head coach, [the] first call I’d make is to the 49ers and say, ‘How much is it going to take to get Kyle Shanahan? Because I think he’s that good. And yes, I’ve always believed this, but coaching matters and it has an impact on an organization.”

It’s not tampering because Aikman currently isn’t running a team. (It could technically be “tampering light” if he’s still working for the Dolphins.) And the information gives Shanahan plenty of leverage in his dealings with the 49ers, if Aikman joins the likes of Matt Millen, John Lynch, and John Elway as former players with little or no front-office experience who find themselves working in high-level jobs with a team.

Aikman has previously made similar comments about Shanahan, in the context of the Bears’ latest coaching vacancy.

“There has been discussion about, ‘Do you give up some picks and see if you can maybe make a deal for a guy like Kyle Shanahan?’” Aikman said during a game in 2024. “ I would be all in on that . Because he would develop a quarterback, and he’s a hell of a head coach. But can you pull that off? That’s a better question. And who might you hire that has no head-coaching experience as an offensive guy? You never know the answer to that, as to how good they’re gonna be.”

While it seems to be working out pretty well for the Bears and their head coach who had no head-coaching experience, the point remains that Aikman would try to hire Shanahan, if Aikman is ever in a position to hire a coach.

And there’s one last twist to this story that currently isn’t known. When Aikman was consulting with the Dolphins during their latest search for a G.M. and head coach, did Aikman advise Miami to call about Shanahan? If so, did they?

Shanahan is in his 10th season with the 49ers. He’s taken the team to two Super Bowls. Barring the franchise’s first championship since 1994 (which could come this year), there could be a point where Shanahan reaches an Andy Reid-style mutual expiration date.

sports.title: Broncos have no comment as to Jim Harbaugh's complaints about Daiyan Henley trade
sports.summary: The failed Daiyan Henley trade has exposed a previously unknown (by many) loophole in the trade deadline, which could be used by an unscrupulous team to leverage better terms after a deal is otherwise done — and the time for negotiating trades has otherwise ended.
sports.body:
Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh essentially accused the Broncos of being unscrupulous by taking the position that Henley had failed his physical but that the physical would magically be un-failed if the compensation for Henley was reduced from a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick.

In response to an inquiry from PFT, the Broncos had no comment on the situation.

During a normal week, Broncos coach Sean Payton would be meeting with reporters on Friday. Because Denver has a Week 10 bye, Payton won’t speak to the media again until Monday.

At that point, it will be interesting to see whether he shares the Broncos’ position, or whether he makes it clear that Denver is moving on.

Of course, that doesn’t stop the Broncos from pushing their position on an off-the-record basis to one of the reporters who routinely covers the team. And their position seems to be that the Broncos believe the Chargers weren’t candid about the condition of Henley’s knee during the discussions that preceded the trade.

The Broncos also contend, not on the record (yet), that the goal was to acquire Henley (who is in the last year of his contract) not as a rental but as a long-term addition. (They would have acquired exclusive negotiating rights with Henley through the opening of the legal tampering period in March.)

Still, with Harbaugh making his case on the record, the Broncos should do the same. While there’s surely some sensitivity to the impact of the chatter about Henley’s knee on his future earning potential, the options (in our view) should be to address the situation on the record or say nothing.

Through it all, the more important point is that the league’s procedures allow things like this to happen. And, apparently, deadline deals have indeed been tweaked in the past based on concerns about a player’s physical.

sports.title: Jesse Minter: Injuries like Lamar Jackson's typically take 6-10 weeks to heal
sports.summary: In an unusual move, the Ravens released a written statement from their head coach to update the quarterback's injury status.
sports.body:
“Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8,” Minter said in the statement the Ravens published on social media and the team’s website. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the the season. second half of the season.”

It’s unclear why the Ravens decided to release this statement, this way. NFL teams rarely announce injury news via a written statement from the head coach. Typically if there’s something to update, the coach will say it at his regularly scheduled press conference, or the player himself will say how he’s doing. In more complex cases, a written statement might come from the team’s medical staff, but not the head coach.

Jackson suffered the injury in Week 8, which means that the 6-10 week timeline would but his return somewhere in the Week 14 to Week 18 neighborhood. Realistically, the Ravens may not be in playoff contention by the time Jackson is cleared to return, which means Jackson’s 2026 season may be over.

sports.title: Falcons announce two-year contract extension with C.J. Henderson
sports.summary: Falcons cornerback C.J.
sports.body:
The Falcons announced today that Henderson has signed a two-year extension.

This is Henderson’s second season on the Falcons, but last year he was mostly a practice squad player who was only active for four games. This year, Henderson has started the last six games at boundary corner after A.J. Terrell went on injured reserve, and Henderson has played very well in his place. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich praised Henderson for how well he has played after being thrust into a new role.

“It’s been a fun journey with C.J. because when he got here, obviously, he had a very well-known past in this league,” Ulbrich said, via the Falcons’ website. “To help him start to reinvent himself here , it brings me a ton of joy because he’s just such an amazing young man. I’m excited for every opportunity he gets and every opportunity to show this league exactly who he is now, today.”

The 28-year-old Henderson entered the NFL with the Jaguars as the ninth overall pick in the 2020 draft. He was a disappointment in Jacksonville and got traded to the Panthers during his second season, and for most of his NFL career he has been viewed as a draft bust. But he got a big opportunity in Atlanta when Terrell went down, and he’s made the most of it. Now he’s getting rewarded.

sports.title: Buccaneers have more rushing yards than passing yards, a rare feat in today's NFL
sports.summary: With the 2026 NFL season at the midway point, one of the bigger statistical oddities belongs to the Buccaneers, who are the only team in the league with more rushing yards than passing yards.
sports.body:
Through nine games, the Buccaneers have 1,475 rushing yards and 1,277 passing yards. Every other team has gained more yardage passing than running, and no other team is even close to having more rushing than passing yards.

The last time an NFL team finished a season with more rushing yards than passing yards was 2022, when the Bears finished with an NFL-high 3,014 rushing yards and an NFL-low 2,219 passing yards. That Bears team was led by Justin Fields, who rushed for 1,143 yards himself, but netted just 1,883 passing yards. With running back David Montgomery chipping in 801 rushing yards and Khalil Herbert gaining 731, the Bears were a team that could run effectively but couldn’t pass for anything.

The Buccaneers’ yardage totals come from some fairly unique circumstances. Baker Mayfield has played some of the worst football of his career when healthy, and he was also injured and missed three games, replaced by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. That has led the Bucs to rely more on their running game. And the weather contributed a huge portion of the Buccaneers’ run-pass yardage differential in Week 8, when the Bucs gained 322 yards rushing and minus-2 yards passing in a downpour against the Falcons.

Despite their one-dimensional offense, the Buccaneers are still playoff contenders, thanks to the NFC South’s status as the worst division in football. It won’t be surprising if there’s a playoff game in Tampa in January. If that happens, Bucs fans may be praying for another downpour.

sports.body: Look at that. Former New York Jets defensive back Jim Leonhard is the defensive coordinator for the Buffalo Bills. Leonhard played for the Jets from 2009 through 2011. sports.title: Bruce Arians says he wants to be a head coach in the NFL next season
sports.summary: Bruce Arians is thinking about coming out of retirement.
sports.body:
Arians told Jordan Schultz that when he announced his retirement from the Buccaneers in March of 2022, it was because of health problems that have since been resolved, and he now wants to coach again.

“I had torn my Achilles early in that season, and I was wearing these prosthetic high heels, and it threw my back out, and I couldn’t stand on the sideline for four hours anymore without a lot of pain,” Arians said. “I was also monitoring an aneurysm on my heart, so I had some health issues. We did everything we thought we could do in Tampa after winning the Super Bowl, trying to get two, and then it was time to give it to Todd [Bowles]. Now that I’m all healthy again, I got the itch again. So, we’ll see.”

If Arians does come back next year, he’ll be the oldest head coach in NFL history. That distinction currently belongs to Pete Carroll, who was 74 when he coached the Raiders last season. Arians will turn 75 next season.

Arians’ first retirement announcement came from the Steelers after they did not renew his contract as their offensive coordinator following the 2011 season, but Arians later said he was forced out and didn’t want to retire. He then took a job as offensive coordinator of the Colts in 2012, and was their interim head coach for most of that season while Chuck Pagano battled leukemia. Arians coached so well that he was named the NFL’s Coach of the Year.

Once Pagano returned to the Colts, Arians became head coach of the Cardinals, and he won a second Coach of the Year award. He announced his retirement following the 2017 season, after five years as head coach of the Cardinals.

But in 2019 he came out of retirement to become head coach of the Buccaneers. He won a Super Bowl in Tampa Bay, then retired after three seasons. Arians thought that was it, but he said that his son is now coaching high school football, and in talking to his son about the job he realized how much he misses it himself.

“Another fire got lit,” Arians said. “I had no desire to go back, and I was still fighting some health issues, but now after the open heart surgery I’ve got so much more energy, it’s amazing.”

Arians may find, like Bill Belichick before him, that all the accomplishments in the world don’t guarantee an NFL head-coaching job. Or perhaps he’ll convince some owner to give the oldest coach ever a chance to do what he’s done three times before, and turn a franchise around.

sports.title: Luke McCaffrey knew the rules and made a heads-up play, causing a kickoff out of bounds
sports.summary: Commanders kickoff returner Luke McCaffrey made the smartest play of the game by not returning a kick in Thursday night's win over the Giants.
sports.body:
With McCaffrey back to field a Giants kickoff, the ball landed near the sideline at the 5-yard line. The kick stayed in bounds, and some returners would have grabbed the ball and started running. But McCaffrey let the ball bounce, then stepped out of bounds, and then grabbed the ball with his feet down on the sideline.

By rule, the ball is out of bounds if it touches a player who is out of bounds, even if the ball actually stays in bounds. By touching the ball while his feet were out of bounds, McCaffrey forced a kickoff out of bounds penalty on the Giants, putting the ball on the 40-yard line for the Commanders.

“I thought Luke McCaffrey made a really smart play that won’t show up on the stat sheet,” Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said. “That’s a difficult play. Is it out of bounds? Is it not? I was nervous about it, that’s one of the ones where you hold your breath.”

Every kickoff returner needs to know that rule, but knowing the rule is easier than having the quick-thinking ability to do what McCaffrey did, in the fourth quarter with the game on the line. It was among the smartest football plays you’ll see.

After the win, the Commanders are 3-5-1, two games behind the division-leading Giants, and the Commanders now own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants. Quinn’s team is still a long shot to win the NFC East, but given the state of that division, it’s not unreasonable to think the Commanders can compete.

And compete is what they did on Thursday night, in a game that went down to the final minute, just as Quinn said the Commanders expected.

“Going into it, we thought this is going to be all four quarters,” Quinn said. “It felt like the most adversity, but also the most belief. It was a balance of both, and we definitely needed that.”

sports.title: John Harbaugh expresses confidence in K Dominic Zvada
sports.summary: Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada has missed six field goals in nine games.
sports.body:
While it happened in the first quarter and not on the final play, it stands out in a game that was decided by three points.

After New York’s 24-21 loss to the Commanders, Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked about his level of confidence in Zvada.

“ Yeah, we’re confident ,” Harbaugh said. “You know, you can’t — as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, I mean, start firing people left and right. Especially your kicker who’s a rookie. So I’m confident that he’s gonna become a good kicker. I mean, if at some point in time, it doesn’t happen, it doesn’t happen.

“But I’m not gonna panic, you know, halfway through the season when the guy who’s made a bunch of kicks, if that’s what you’re inferring we should be doing. So, you know, I mean, we’re just not gonna knee-jerk it like that. He’s gonna make kicks. He’s gonna make a lot of kicks, I believe in him. I think he’s really good, really talented. And we’re gonna give him an opportunity to do it. It’s up to him to do it.”

That’s a fair assessment of a player who’s still new to the NFL. But a kicker has one job. If he can’t do it (especially from distances that should be automatic), at some point tough questions need to be asked.

Basically, how much time will Zvada get before Harbaugh decides it’s not going to happen? That remains to be seen, if Zvada keeps missing kicks he should be making.

sports.title: Thursday Night Football: Stefon Diggs' late TD gives Commanders 24-21 win
sports.summary: The wide receiver caught a 32-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 57 seconds left.
sports.body:
The Commanders got the last laugh, winning 24-21 on Stefon Diggs’ 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The Commanders are 3-5-1 and the Giants 5-3-1.

In an entertaining second half, the teams traded the lead four times.

The Giants took a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left on Isaiah Likely’s 66-yard catch-and-run.

The Giants then had back-to-back interceptions of Jayden Daniels. Safety Jevon Holland, who is having an All-Pro season, took the ball away from Chig Okonkwo at the 2-yard line with the Commanders on the Giants 24 with 5:27 left, and Ar’Darius Washington stepped in front of Okonkwo on fourth-and-2 at the Washington 45 with 2:15 left.

The Giants, though, couldn’t run out the clock, and the Commanders made the most of it. They needed only three plays to go 71 yards thanks to a questionable 33-yard pass interference penalty on Deonte Banks, who was covering Treylon Burks. Three plays later, Diggs scored.

The Giants reached the Washington 48 on their final drive, but J.J. McCarthy’s deep throw to Malik Nabers was intercepted by Rasul Douglas with 25 seconds left to end it.

The Giants outgained the Commanders 399 to 340, but missed a field goal and had two turnovers.

Daniels was 23-of-33 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Rachaad White ran for 47 yards on 11 carries, and Diggs caught six passes for 83 yards. Antonio Williams and Ben Sinnott each caught a touchdown pass.

No pressure, I’m not worried about it. I’ve been playing football since I was five, six years old. They come in bunches. They’ll come eventually so just keep doing what I need to do to help this team. When they present themselves, hopefully hold the ball and take advantage of it.”

On Sunday, Donald finally played with Myles Garrett, the player whose arrival in June sparked Donald’s decision to return after two years of retirement. Garrett, in his first game since Week 1, had 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble.

Regardless, the Rams won, pushing themselves above .500 for the first time this year. On Sunday at Arizona, they have a chance to win their fourth in a row.

And Donald has another chance to get his first sack since he returned from retirement.

sports.title: Justin Jefferson: It's a joy to see Kirk Cousins take over as a leader

sports.body:
The wide receiver had career highs in catches (128) and yards (1,809) and earned the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award in Cousins’ last full season with the Vikings in 2022.

“It’s really just going out there and just executing our plays ,” Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN. “It’s not really getting too juiced up about him being here or anybody being back there. It’s just all about understanding the plays that are being called, understanding the jobs that we have and executing our responsibilities. And just the plays that are there, and the plays that could be made, we just need to continue to just make those type of plays. And I’m pretty sure that the results would be a lot better.

“He just understands the game. He’s a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throw those type of plays, but he also doesn’t force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me.”

Jefferson said it was “a joy to hear [Cousins] just take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field.”

“He’s being vocal,” Jefferson said. “Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he’s talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he’s just making sure that everybody’s on the same page. So it’s definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that’s pretty normal from him. So it’s definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking that control.”

sports.title: DeMarvion Overshown didn't know inactive players couldn't celebrate on the field
sports.summary: The Cowboys had 14 accepted penalties for 153 yards in the 27-23 win over the Colts.
sports.body:
Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who was inactive and dressed in street clothes, came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We have non-uniformed player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty.”

Overshown apologized to head coach Brian Schottenheimer and his teammates.

“At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it,” Overshown said Thursday, via Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News . “I apologized about it. It was definitely in the moment, but earlier I had said that as a defense, we’re going to start celebrating more, getting takeaways. And I was just caught in the moment. So you can laugh at it now, because we won the game, but in the moment, fourth quarter, tied ball game or close ball game, you don’t want a 15-yard penalty from a guy, especially that’s not even playing. So that’s a lesson learned.”

Overshown said he didn’t know the rule until linebacker Dee Winters started yelling at him, which should prompt questions about why Overshown didn’t know the rule. But he defended Schottenheimer and said he accepted his “butt chewing.”

“It’s not an indictment on Schotty. It’s on me as a player. I own it,” he said.
